key_insight: A DSL-grounded multi-agent LLM system can improve inverse design by translating natural-language materials rules into symbolic predicates that are statistically checked and refined during search.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical route to faster, more interpretable discovery of high-performance materials, reducing reliance on large task-specific datasets or custom model training.
method: Builds symbolic predicates from natural-language design rules using a chemistry DSL.
Uses accumulated materials data to test, validate, or reject candidate rules during iterative LLM reasoning.
Runs a multi-agent inverse-design loop (ORCHESTRA) to search double perovskite oxides for multiple target properties.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the DSL-guided framework improved materials design performance versus natural-language-only rules, especially for harder target properties, and helped identify unsupported or newly validated rules across iterative cycles.
watch_item: Performance gains are described at a high level in the abstract, so practical impact may depend on the quality of the DSL, the available materials database, and how well the rule store generalizes beyond double perovskites.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
